component.name: Soundscape
component.summary: Scrobble to your own music tracker

description.p: Soundscape Desktop is the Linux app for Soundscape, a music tracker you host yourself. It shows your Soundscape server in its own window and sends what you play on your computer, in any music player, to your listening history.

ul.li: Picks up what Spotify, Strawberry, Rhythmbox, Elisa and other players are playing, with no plugins
Counts a play once you've heard half the song or four minutes, like ListenBrainz and Last.fm
Lets you love the song that's playing, or keep it out of your history, from the tray
Remembers fixes for players that send wrong or messy song names
Pauses scrobbling for an hour and turns it back on by itself
Tidies up the names of untagged music files, like "03 - Artist - Song.flac"
Shows today's plays, listening time and your streak in the tray
Can remind you in the evening before your listening streak ends
Tells you in December when your Yearscape for the year is ready
Has a small mini player that stays on top and controls any music player
Keeps plays while your server is offline and sends them with their original times later
Leaves browsers out unless you turn them on, and then counts only songs, with titles like "(Official Video)" cleaned up
Shows new followers, friends passing you on the weekly leaderboard and play milestones as notifications
Shows who you follow is playing right now and plays their song with one click, and sums up your week every Monday
Lets media keys and your desktop's media controls play and pause song previews
Finds your artists and songs from GNOME's search and KDE's KRunner
Can start when you log in and keep scrobbling in the background

description.p: You need your own Soundscape server. The app connects with its own token, which you can see and revoke on the server.

Scrobbling, players and notifications in one place

ul.li: Prevent normal restarts and quick closes from falsely turning CPU rendering on
Keep the player volume when closing and reopening the main window
Load album art in MPRIS media bars and Discord Rich Presence on self-hosted and Tailscale servers
Add a helper script to recolor the Flatpak launcher icon with the accent color
The window, tray and mini player icons can take the accent color, turned on in Settings
The mini player's visualizer and controls follow the accent color picked in Settings
The visualizer updates more often, so the bars move more smoothly
The visualizer has more headroom, so loud songs no longer keep the bars at the top
A real-time audio spectrum visualizer in the player bar and the mini player that reacts to the music, with its style, bounciness and bands picked in Settings
A scrollbar on the right edge of the window shows where you are on long pages and lets you click or drag to jump
Scrolling the mouse wheel over volume and seek bars now adjusts them directly
The memory threshold for loading pages fresh now counts only private memory, ignoring shared GPU driver mappings
Pressing Esc now closes the Ctrl+K quick finder and confirmation dialogs, and the finder draws cleanly above page elements
Copying text, tokens and share links now works reliably on Wayland and X11
Text and password boxes on Connect, Login, Sign up and Settings now span the full form width
Clickable song, artist and album links in the player bar now work for unplayed Navidrome tracks
Back, forward and home buttons now work and show up correctly in dark mode
Artist pages show every album and song from your Navidrome library, not just ones you've played
Playing from an artist page now works for collaborations like "Artist • Other Artist"
Lower background memory usage: the web window now runs as its own process, so the background daemon no longer loads the browser engine when the window is closed
Reduced memory usage while open through tighter browser, media and thread limits, a shared D-Bus connection and HTTP client, and freeing mini player buffers when hidden
Lighter mini player font loading using memory-mapped fonts with lazy fallback for CJK text

Tighter security across the app: messages from the window are only accepted from your Soundscape server, the built-in player's local relay validates requests strictly and shuts down cleanly, and dialogs escape text safely
File pickers and dialogs fall back to kdialog when zenity isn't installed
More reliable scrobbling, Discord Rich Presence, live playback updates, autostart setup and window reopening, with race conditions and retry bugs fixed
Shuffle works in the built-in player, from the player bar and the mini player (needs an up-to-date Soundscape server)
Turning shuffle off puts the songs still to come back in their original order
Keep playing similar music no longer stops after a few songs you hadn't played before
The radio no longer adds the song that's playing, or songs already in the queue, a second time
Picks are based on artists that sound alike, from ListenBrainz and Deezer (needs an up-to-date Soundscape server)
With Keep playing similar music turned on in Soundscape's player settings, the built-in player starts a radio from the last song when the queue runs out, and tops it up as it plays
Other devices see changes to the queue sooner
A new setting under Starting and closing keeps the window ready for a minute, 5 or 15 minutes, always, or closes it right away to save memory
The app keeps your login in your desktop's keyring when one is available, instead of in its settings file
The built-in player's local stream can only be used by the app itself
The mini player shows the artist and album, or "Unknown album" when the album isn't known
Songs started from anywhere in Soundscape now show their album in the mini player, the media controls and the player in the app
The play and pause button changes the moment you press it
Song titles, artists and times in the mini player are the same size as in the app
The mini player uses the same play button, icons, colours and progress bar as the player in the app
Seeking in the mini player no longer jumps back before moving to the new spot
Fonts for the mini player are no longer copied into memory, which used up to a couple of hundred megabytes on systems with large Chinese and Japanese fonts
The mini player is drawn by the app itself, so it uses a few megabytes instead of a few hundred when the main window is closed
Closing and reopening the window within a minute brings it straight back
The player bar slides in only the first time it appears
Seeking while a song is still loading no longer flashes 0:00 first
Quitting from the tray closes the app right away
The window runs separately and is shut down completely when you close it, so the app left running in the background takes a few dozen megabytes instead of several hundred
Music, scrobbling, the tray and notifications keep going while the window is closed, and it opens again where you left off
The player bar no longer slides in again every time you start a song
Seeking moves the progress bar straight to the new spot instead of jumping back first
Media keys and the mini player show the new spot right away too
Music starts at the volume you set in Soundscape instead of a fixed level
Volume levelling and crossfade from Soundscape's player settings now apply, and change as soon as you change them
Your phone and other browsers see what the computer is playing under Devices, and can pause, skip or send music to it
Music plays in the app's own player, so closing or opening the window never interrupts it
Songs that only have a preview play in the app's own player too (needs an up-to-date Soundscape server)
Starting at login only loads the window once you open it, which saves a lot of memory
The window opens at the size you left it, maximised or not
The window uses your desktop's interface font and follows when you change it
Touchpad scrolling follows your fingers directly and coasts to a stop
Back and forward buttons and the version show on the page again
The app now draws its window with the Servo browser engine instead of WebKitGTK
Closing the window frees its graphics memory, and on Wayland the window really closes instead of staying around
While the app's own player carries on the music, the page is set aside completely and comes back where the music is when you open the window
Clicking a notification opens what it is about, like the new follower's profile or your Yearscape
Clicking Soundscape in your desktop's media controls opens the window
Title fixes, changing the server and signing out are now in Soundscape's Settings page, under This app
The tray no longer needs extra libraries, and opening the app a second time brings the running one forward
The window stays silent until it has caught up with the background player, then the two fade over
The two players line up more closely before they switch
Fixes the app closing right after it starts on Wayland desktops that enforce explicit sync, with NVIDIA graphics
The app turns off NVIDIA's explicit sync for itself, which some compositors otherwise refused
If the app ever closes right after starting, the next start tries the other rendering setting and says so
CPU rendering no longer changes how frames reach the screen, which some compositors refused
If the app ever closes right after starting, the next start turns CPU rendering off by itself and says so
Wheel scrolling now speeds up and slows down gradually, even when you turn the wheel quickly
Each turn of the wheel now glides to its place in about a seventh of a second, and quick turns add up
Touchpads scroll as before
Each turn of the wheel now glides instead of jumping
Turn it off with Smooth scrolling under This app on the Settings page, or in the app's own settings window
Pages are now drawn with the processor by default, which keeps scrolling smooth on high refresh rate screens
Turn it off with Enable CPU rendering under This app on the Settings page, or in the app's own settings window
Start the app with SOUNDSCAPE_SHOW_FPS=1 to show frames per second in the corner of the window
Settings (Ctrl+, the menu and the tray) now opens Soundscape's Settings page, where the app's settings are under This app, next to your account and the player
The small settings window is still there for title fixes, changing the server and signing out, and for when the server can't be reached
The app's own settings are now called App settings, and say what is on Soundscape's Settings page instead
Each settings page has a button that opens the other one (Soundscape's needs an up-to-date server)
The version also shows under the Soundscape logo on the home page
Needs an up-to-date Soundscape server
The version is at the bottom of Settings and at the top of the Soundscape menu
When a newer version is out, Settings says so, with a Download button
Songs started from the home page or the feed show their album, looked up on your Soundscape server
When no album is known, the status says Unknown album
The album cover, with the album name when you point at it, and a progress bar with the song's length
Jumping in a song moves the bar, and pausing clears the status
Covers come from the player, or from your Soundscape server when it's on https; otherwise the Soundscape logo
The mini player, media keys and the app's own player use the length your Navidrome reports when the stream doesn't say how long a song is, so the time bar works and these songs count as plays
Open Soundscape is now the first item in the tray menu
Closing the window: the app's player starts quietly in step with the page, then the two cross over in a third of a second, so the music doesn't stop
Opening it again: the app's player keeps playing while the page loads, and the page takes over in step the same way
When you close the window while music plays, the app's own player takes over the same queue at the same second and the page is closed, so the app uses about half the memory
Media keys, the mini player, the tray and Discord keep working, songs still count as plays, and the next song follows without a gap
Open the window again and the page carries on from where the app's player is
Turn it off in Settings to keep the page playing in the background as before

It follows the player you're listening to, and songs played in the Soundscape window
Discord needs an application of your own for this; Settings explains how to make one in a minute
Once a day the app checks the releases on GitHub; when a newer version is out, a notification says so once and the tray gets a "Download Soundscape Desktop …" item that opens the download page
Turn it off in Settings with "Tell me when a new version of this app is out"
Closing the window while a song plays no longer stops it: the window hides, the music keeps going, and the mini player, media keys and tray still control it
Once nothing has played for 5 minutes, the hidden page is closed to free memory, as before
Back, forward and home buttons next to the Soundscape logo in the window, like in a browser

Links to other websites, like an artist's own site or Bandcamp, now open in your web browser, also from the Flatpak and also when they were meant to open in a new tab
A new Go menu with Back (Alt+Left), Forward (Alt+Right) and Home (Alt+Home), like in a browser
Soundscape → Music, also in the tray, opens the Music tab, and each Navidrome playlist can be started from there with one click
The mini player has a seek bar you can click or drag, and shuffle and repeat buttons for players that support them
While a song plays in the Soundscape window, the mini player shows which song is up next in the queue
The Music menu needs an up-to-date Soundscape server
Closing the window now frees most of the memory the page was using while the app keeps scrobbling in the tray
Next and previous in the mini player and on your media keys move through the Soundscape play queue

A mini player (Ctrl+M) stays on top with the cover, play/pause, next, previous and love, for any music player

Pause scrobbling for an hour; it turns back on by itself
